item.title: How to verify running Kicksecure version?
item.dc:creator: user4023
item.description:
Hi Guys, this is TS. I think all by now have given there input and I would like to close this discussion with a short summary.

My orginal question was: how to verify the running Kicksecure(minor) version. The short answer is: that is not possible. Currently only the major version can be found in /etc/kicksecure_version.

Remarks were made about the usefullness of needing to now the exact running minor version since the major version + updates constitutes the latest updated minor version. That is a solid point.

If anyone would like to make a featuture request to show the minor version anywhere, that of course is there prerogative.

With that being said I would like to close this topic and thank all for taking the time to contribute.

Cheers,

catharinewine25315:

Still, a minor version in /etc/kicksecure_version has some diagnostic value even if it can’t prove you’re fully updated: it tells you which snapshot you actually booted, which helps when filing a bug report or comparing two machines.

“Snapshot” isn’t meaningful as Kicksecure doesn’t have a native snapshotting mechanism at the moment. Because package updates happen without point releases sometimes (frequently even), the only way to be sure what software versions you’re running are to check package versions directly using something like dpkg-query -s <package name>.

catharinewine25315:

An EOL warning would arguably be the more useful thing to surface.

EOL warnings are already integrated into Kicksecure.

item.dc:creator: catharinewine25315
item.description:
The point about embedding a point release number only telling you that one package is recent enough is fair, and I think it undercuts the original GUI request. Still, a minor version in /etc/kicksecure_version has some diagnostic value even if it can’t prove you’re fully updated: it tells you which snapshot you actually booted, which helps when filing a bug report or comparing two machines. Combining that with systemcheck seems reasonable—the version file for identification, systemcheck for update status. An EOL warning would arguably be the more useful thing to surface.

item.title: How to verify running Kicksecure version?
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
I’m not sure how this could be done in a way that is particularly valuable. Knowing the build version you are effectively running might be useful to ensure you aren’t missing updates, but embedding the latest point release version into a package won’t do that, all it will do is tell you that you have a new enough version of that specific package installed. The best way to tell if you have all updates installed is to run systemcheck, which will tell you if you have Kicksecure repos enabled and if there are any updates available. If you have Kicksecure repos enabled and there are no updates available, then you have everything installed and don’t need to worry (unless of course you’re running an EOL major version of Kicksecure). I’m not sure what other use an updating build version number would have.

Kicksecure – 13 May 26

Point Release

What is a Point Release?

Installing any version of Kicksecure 18 and fully updating it leads to a system which is (mostly) identical to installing a Kicksecure point release.

If the Kicksecure installation is updated, no further action is required.
